source_evidence.observation: Throughout the paper, A is m by n, SA is s by n, m > s > n, and both A and SA have full rank.
Sketch-and-apply forms B = SA, obtains R by Householder QR, computes Y = A R^{-1} with forward substitution, solves Yz = b by unpreconditioned LSQR, and recovers x by back substitution.
For economized QR factorizations A = Q_A R_A and SA = QR, the exact-arithmetic preconditioned matrix satisfies kappa_2(A R^{-1}) = kappa_2(S Q_A).
The paper assumes finite-precision computations with unit roundoff u much smaller than one and identifies the matrix 2-norm in its error bounds as the spectral norm.
For nonsingular upper triangular R, the paper describes computing A R^{-1} row by row by solving R^T x_i = a_i with substitution.

source_evidence.anchor: Opening of Section 3 and its three numbered finite-precision stages
source_evidence.observation: The computed stages are B_hat = SA + E_1, Q_tilde R_hat = B_hat + E_2, and Y_hat = A R_hat^{-1} + DeltaY; hats indicate rounding errors.

Lemma 3.1 defines the exact QR factors, computed B_hat and R_hat, E = Q_tilde R_hat - QR, and epsilon_1 = ||E||_2 ||R^{-1}||_2; under epsilon_1 < 1, R_hat is invertible and A R_hat^{-1} has full rank.
The inherited bound is kappa_2(A R_hat^{-1}) <= kappa_2(S Q_A)(1 + epsilon_1)/(1 - epsilon_1).

For Y_hat computed from A R_hat^{-1} by forward substitution, DeltaY = Y_hat - A R_hat^{-1} and epsilon_2 = ||DeltaY||_2 ||(A R_hat^{-1})^dagger||_2. If epsilon_2 < 1, Y_hat has full rank and kappa_2(Y_hat) <= (kappa_2(A R_hat^{-1}) + epsilon_2)/(1 - epsilon_2). The dagger denotes the matrix pseudoinverse.

binders: Dimensions m, s, n satisfy m > s > n; A is in R^{m x n}, S is in R^{s x m}, and SA is in R^{s x n}. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, standing-assumptions paragraph]
A = Q_A R_A and SA = QR are economized QR factorizations, with R in R^{n x n}. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 916, Lemma 3.1]
B_hat is the finite-precision result of forming SA, and R_hat in R^{n x n} is the upper triangular factor computed by Householder QR of B_hat. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 916, Lemma 3.1]
Y_hat and DeltaY are m by n matrices, with Y_hat obtained by finite-precision forward substitution applied to A R_hat^{-1}. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
hypotheses: A and SA have full column rank n under the standing dimensions. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, standing-assumptions paragraph]

R_hat^{-1} is the inverse arising from the Lemma 3.1 setup; Lemma 3.1 assumes epsilon_1 < 1 and thereby establishes that R_hat is invertible and A R_hat^{-1} has full column rank. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 916, Lemma 3.1]
Y_hat is computed from A R_hat^{-1} using forward substitution in finite precision. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
The explicit hypothesis of Lemma 3.2 is epsilon_2 < 1. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
conclusions: Y_hat has full rank, hence rank n because Y_hat is m by n with m > n. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2; PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, standing dimensions]
kappa_2(Y_hat) <= (kappa_2(A R_hat^{-1}) + epsilon_2)/(1 - epsilon_2). [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
definitions_and_conventions: DeltaY is defined exactly as Y_hat - A R_hat^{-1}; its reference matrix uses the computed QR factor R_hat, not the exact factor R. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
epsilon_2 is defined exactly as ||DeltaY||_2 ||(A R_hat^{-1})^dagger||_2. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
The dagger superscript denotes the matrix pseudoinverse. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, footnote 3]
Hats denote quantities for which rounding errors are being accounted for. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 916, opening of Section 3]
For a tall m by n matrix in this setting, full rank means full column rank n. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, standing dimensions and rank assumptions]
implicit_context: Lemma 3.1 defines E = Q_tilde R_hat - QR and epsilon_1 = ||E||_2 ||R^{-1}||_2; epsilon_1 < 1 is the inherited route by which R_hat^{-1} and the full-rank reference matrix A R_hat^{-1} are available. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 916, Lemma 3.1]

Lemma 3.1 additionally gives kappa_2(A R_hat^{-1}) <= kappa_2(S Q_A)(1 + epsilon_1)/(1 - epsilon_1), but Lemma 3.2 leaves kappa_2(A R_hat^{-1}) unexpanded in its conclusion. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, continuation of Lemma 3.1 and Lemma 3.2]
In exact arithmetic with the exact QR factor R, kappa_2(A R^{-1}) = kappa_2(S Q_A). [PDF p. 9, printed p. 913, Lemma 2.1]

Although Algorithm 1.3 draws a random sketch, Lemma 3.2 is a deterministic perturbation statement and contains no probability or distributional conclusion. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3; PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Lemma 3.2 analyzes step 4 of the sketch-and-apply algorithm: explicit finite-precision formation of the preconditioned matrix before unpreconditioned LSQR. It does not analyze repeated right-preconditioner applications, nor does it itself assert accuracy or backward stability of the later LSQR solution or recovered x. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3; PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
numerical_model: The surrounding numerical model assumes precision u much smaller than one and says arithmetic is exact up to that precision. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 914, Section 2.3]
The three relevant computed stages are B_hat = SA + E_1, Q_tilde R_hat = B_hat + E_2, and Y_hat = A R_hat^{-1} + DeltaY. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 916, opening of Section 3]

Forward substitution corresponds in the surrounding derivation to row-wise triangular solves R^T x_i = a_i; for the selected result, the factor is R_hat. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 915, Section 2.3.3; PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]

Lemma 3.2 does not contain an explicit formula in u, gamma_n, or componentwise rounding errors; it abstracts all triangular-solve error into DeltaY and epsilon_2. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
error_notions: DeltaY is an additive forward error relative to the exact mathematical matrix A R_hat^{-1} formed from the computed factor R_hat. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]

epsilon_2 scales ||DeltaY||_2 by ||(A R_hat^{-1})^dagger||_2, so the perturbation is measured relative to the smallest singular-value scale of the reference matrix. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2 and footnote 3]

The result controls rank preservation and the spectral condition number; it does not state a least-squares residual, forward solution error, normal residual, or normwise backward-error bound. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
norms: Every norm displayed in the definition of epsilon_2 and in the condition number is the matrix 2-norm; the paper identifies this as the spectral norm. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 914, equation (2.2); PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
The paper defines kappa_2 by the largest singular value divided by the smallest singular value. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, discussion following Algorithm 1.1]
The pseudoinverse in epsilon_2 is the matrix pseudoinverse. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, footnote 3]
No Frobenius norm occurs in Lemma 3.2. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
constants_and_indexing: The threshold is the strict inequality epsilon_2 < 1. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
The numerator is exactly kappa_2(A R_hat^{-1}) + epsilon_2 and the denominator is exactly 1 - epsilon_2; both coefficients of epsilon_2 are one. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]

The formal standing dimension inequalities are m > s > n; the algorithmic notation m much greater than s is informal and supplies no additional numerical threshold. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, standing assumptions; PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3]
Lemma 3.2 contains no summation indices, iteration indices, or index offsets. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
higher_order_terms: The Lemma 3.2 bound contains no big-O term and no omitted higher-order term; it is stated directly in terms of epsilon_2. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]

The subsequent prose says the triangular-solve error is small under kappa_2(A)u much smaller than one, but that qualitative condition is not an explicit hypothesis of Lemma 3.2. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, paragraph following Lemma 3.2]
exceptional_values: The inherited epsilon_1 < 1 condition makes R_hat invertible, so R_hat^{-1} is defined. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 916, Lemma 3.1]
Because epsilon_2 is a product of norms, it is nonnegative; together with epsilon_2 < 1 this makes 1 - epsilon_2 positive. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, definition and hypothesis in Lemma 3.2]

The cited floating-point setup and Lemma 3.2 do not explicitly state assumptions about overflow, underflow, subnormal values, NaNs, infinities, or a particular rounding mode. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 914, Section 2.3; PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]

undebatable_constraints: The reference matrix in DeltaY and epsilon_2 is A R_hat^{-1}, using the computed Householder-QR factor, not A R^{-1} using the exact QR factor. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]

Y_hat must be the finite-precision forward-substitution result for A R_hat^{-1}; the source does not define it as an arbitrary perturbation unrelated to that computation. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
DeltaY = Y_hat - A R_hat^{-1} and epsilon_2 = ||DeltaY||_2 ||(A R_hat^{-1})^dagger||_2 exactly. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
The hypothesis is epsilon_2 < 1, with a strict inequality. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
Both conclusions must be retained: Y_hat has full column rank and satisfies the stated condition-number bound. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
The condition-number bound is kappa_2(Y_hat) <= (kappa_2(A R_hat^{-1}) + epsilon_2)/(1 - epsilon_2), with no altered constants, powers, or index shifts. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
All norms in epsilon_2 are spectral 2-norms, and the dagger is the matrix pseudoinverse. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 914, equation (2.2); PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2 and footnote 3]
The hard dimensional context is A in R^{m x n}, S in R^{s x m}, m > s > n, with A and SA full column rank. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, standing-assumptions paragraph]
Lemma 3.2 is deterministic and does not require a specified sketch distribution or assert a probabilistic bound. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]

No explicit u-dependent smallness condition, big-O remainder, LSQR convergence claim, or final-solution backward-error claim belongs to Lemma 3.2 itself. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2 and following paragraph]

contract_plain_english: For full-column-rank A and SA with dimensions m > s > n, form the sketch and its Householder-QR factor in finite precision, obtaining the computed upper triangular R_hat. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, standing assumptions; PDF p. 12, printed p. 916, Lemma 3.1] Compute Y_hat as the finite-precision forward-substitution result for A R_hat^{-1}, and define DeltaY = Y_hat - A R_hat^{-1} and epsilon_2 = ||DeltaY||_2 ||(A R_hat^{-1})^dagger||_2. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2] If epsilon_2 < 1, then Y_hat retains full column rank and kappa_2(Y_hat) is at most (kappa_2(A R_hat^{-1}) + epsilon_2)/(1 - epsilon_2). [PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2] This is a deterministic spectral-norm perturbation result for the matrix-formation stage of sketch-and-apply, not by itself a claim about LSQR convergence or final least-squares backward stability. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3; PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2]
